posts.post_title: NDV is classified in which viral genus?
posts.post_content: The causative agent of Newcastle disease is classified in which viral genus?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Avulavirus

Newcastle disease virus is Paramyxovirus type 1, placed in genus Avulavirus.

Correct Option Explanation

It belongs to family Paramyxoviridae, genus Avulavirus, as PMV-1.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Orthomyxovirus is the genus of avian influenza viruses, not NDV.
  • Alphaherpesvirus is the subfamily containing Marek's disease virus.
  • Circovirus is the genus of chicken infectious anaemia virus.
Know More
  • NDV pathotypes range from lentogenic to viscerotropic velogenic.
  • First outbreak recorded in 1926 in Java, Indonesia.
  • Doyle named it after Newcastle-upon-Tyne, England, in 1927.
  • B1 and LaSota strains are common live vaccines.

posts.post_title: In India, ND was first recorded in 1927 at…
posts.post_content: In India, Newcastle disease was first recorded in 1927 at Ranikhet in which region, giving the disease its alternate name?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:

Edward first recorded the disease at Ranikhet, Nainital District, in 1927, giving rise to the name Ranikhet disease.

  • Vidarbha, Malabar and Saurashtra are not linked to the naming of Ranikhet disease.
Know More
  • The disease was first described worldwide in 1926 in Java, Indonesia.
  • Doyle described the disease in Newcastle-upon-Tyne in 1927.

  • Chickens are the most susceptible domestic poultry species.

posts.post_title: How many pathotypes of NDV are recognised…
posts.post_content: Based on the disease produced in chickens, how many pathotypes of Newcastle disease virus are recognised?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Five

Five pathotypes of NDV are recognised based on disease severity in chickens.

Correct Option Explanation

They are viscerotropic velogenic, neurotropic velogenic, mesogenic, lentogenic, and asymptomatic enteric strains.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Three, four and six are simple miscounts of the five listed pathotypes.
Know More
  • Viscerotropic velogenic strains cause haemorrhagic intestinal lesions.
  • Lentogenic strains cause mild or inapparent respiratory infection.
  • Mesogenic strains cause low mortality with respiratory signs.
  • Asymptomatic strains cause inapparent enteric infection only.

posts.post_title: Mortality of velogenic NDV infection is…
posts.post_content: What is the approximate mortality rate associated with velogenic (highly virulent) Newcastle disease virus infection?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 100%

Velogenic NDV strains typically cause mortality approaching 100% in susceptible flocks.

Correct Option Explanation

Clinical signs include sudden death, prostration, diarrhoea and cyanosis of the comb, with mortality reaching 100%.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • 50% is the mortality typically seen with mesogenic (moderately virulent) strains.
  • 10% and 25% do not match either velogenic or mesogenic figures given.
Know More
  • Mesogenic strains cause severe respiratory signs with egg-production drop.
  • Lentogenic strains cause only mild, short-lived respiratory signs.
  • Onset of clinical signs averages 5 days post exposure.
  • Nervous system lesions are absent regardless of pathotype.

posts.post_title: Two lentogenic strains used as live ND vac…
posts.post_content: Which two lentogenic strains are most widely used as live Newcastle disease vaccines?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: B1 and LaSota

B1 and LaSota lentogenic strains are the chief live ND vaccines used.

Correct Option Explanation

They are typically administered by mass application in drinking water or by spray to poultry flocks.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Rispens and SB-1 are Marek's disease vaccine strains, not NDV.
  • H120 and H52, and F and Ulster, are not the ND strains named in the source.
Know More
  • Oil-adjuvanted inactivated vaccines are also used in breeders and layers.
  • Chicks are vaccinated as early as day 1-4 of life.
  • Delaying vaccination avoids maternal antibody interference with immunity.
  • Live mesogenic strain vaccines may be used in older birds where permitted.

posts.post_title: Standard confirmation test for ND is…
posts.post_content: Which serological test is considered the standard confirmation test for Newcastle disease through demonstration of a rising antibody titre in paired sera?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Haemagglutination-inhibition test

A rise in haemagglutination-inhibition antibodies in paired serum samples confirms Newcastle disease.

Correct Option Explanation

The HI test is described as the confirmation test, alongside other serological tests and virus isolation.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Agar gel precipitin and virus neutralisation are listed as other serological options, not the confirmation test.
  • ELISA is described as popular for flock screening, not the confirmation test.
Know More
  • Definitive diagnosis needs virus isolation and monoclonal antibody characterisation.
  • Cloacal or tracheal swabs are collected from live birds.
  • No NDV clinical sign or lesion is regarded as pathognomonic.
  • ND must be differentiated from infectious bronchitis and avian influenza.

posts.post_title: IBD was first reported at Gumboro in which…
posts.post_content: Infectious bursal disease was first reported in poultry raised in which locality, giving the disease its common name 'Gumboro disease'?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:

Infectious bursal disease was first reported in Gumboro, Delaware District, USA.

Correct Option Explanation

This first report gave the disease its widely used common name, Gumboro disease.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Ranikhet and Newcastle relate to the naming of Newcastle disease, not IBD.

Know More
  • Other names include infectious bursitis and avian nephrosis (1962).

posts.post_title: IBDV belongs to which family and genome…
posts.post_content: The causative virus of infectious bursal disease belongs to which virus family and genome type?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Birnaviridae, double-stranded RNA

Infectious bursal disease virus is a Birnavirus with a double-stranded RNA genome.

Correct Option Explanation

The name Birna reflects its bisegmented, double-stranded RNA genome ('Birna' = two).

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Circoviridae with single-stranded DNA describes chicken infectious anaemia virus, not IBDV.
  • Reoviridae and Picornaviridae are unrelated families used as distractor entities here.
Know More
  • Serotype 1 IBDV causes up to 50% mortality in chickens.
  • Serotype 2 IBDV is not pathogenic or immunosuppressive.
  • The virus is highly resistant, surviving up to 122 days in poultry houses.
  • No vertical transmission or true carrier state is described.

posts.post_title: The primary target cells of IBDV are…
posts.post_content: The primary target cells of infectious bursal disease virus are:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: B-lymphocytes

B-lymphocytes and their precursors are the main target cells of IBDV.

Correct Option Explanation

Their depletion in the bursa causes severe, often permanent immunosuppression in young chickens.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • T-lymphocytes are relatively unaffected by IBDV infection.
  • Macrophages and erythrocytes are not described as the primary IBDV target cells.
Know More
  • Bursal infection in early life impairs long-term immune responses.
  • Immunosuppression predisposes birds to vaccination failure and E. coli infection.
  • It also predisposes to gangrenous dermatitis and inclusion body hepatitis.
  • Chemical bursectomy with cyclophosphamide confers resistance to challenge.

posts.post_title: Which statement about serotype 2 IBDV is…
posts.post_content: Which statement about serotype 2 infectious bursal disease virus is correct?

_aimcq_options.text: It is widespread but not pathogenic or immunosuppressive
It causes up to 50% mortality in chickens
It has strong tropism for B-lymphocytes of the bursa
It is restricted to chickens only

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: It is widespread but not pathogenic or immunosuppressive

Serotype 2 IBDV is widely distributed but causes no disease or immunosuppression.

Correct Option Explanation

It affects chickens, turkeys and ducks without producing clinical disease, unlike serotype 1.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • 50% mortality and strong bursal B-lymphocyte tropism describe serotype 1 IBDV, not serotype 2.
  • It is not restricted to chickens; it also affects turkeys and ducks.
Know More
  • Serotype 1 shows antigenic variation from apathogenic to highly virulent strains.
  • Both serotypes 1 and 2 infect turkeys and ducks without disease.
  • The bursa is the principal lymphoid organ severely affected.
  • Diagnosis includes AGPT and ELISA on bursal tissue.

posts.post_title: Chickens are most susceptible to IBD at…
posts.post_content: Chickens are most susceptible to clinical infectious bursal disease at what age?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 3-6 weeks

Chicks aged 3-6 weeks are most susceptible to acute infectious bursal disease.

Correct Option Explanation

This age coincides with a well-developed bursa, allowing high mortality following acute infection.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Infection at 1-2 days to under 3 weeks typically causes subclinical immunosuppression instead.
  • Older birds beyond 6 weeks are more resistant owing to bursal regression.
Know More
  • Incubation period of the acute form is 2-3 days.
  • Mortality can reach 90-100% with very virulent IBDV strains.
  • Mortality normally peaks 3-5 days after infection.
  • Older birds resist infection due to bursal regression with age.

posts.post_title: IBDV can remain infectious in the poultry…
posts.post_content: According to its described environmental stability, for how long can infectious bursal disease virus remain highly infectious in the poultry house environment?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Up to 122 days

IBDV remains highly infectious in the poultry environment for up to 122 days.

Correct Option Explanation

The virus is very stable and hardy, surviving heat, cleaning and disinfectant procedures between outbreaks.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • 52 days is the survival period described for water, feed and droppings, not the general environment figure.
  • 14 days and 365 days do not match either stated survival period.
Know More
  • Meal worms and litter mites stay infective for up to 8 weeks.
  • Mechanical vectors include humans, wild birds and insects.
  • Older birds are more resistant owing to bursal regression.
  • No vertical transmission of IBDV has been demonstrated.

posts.post_title: In IBD, bursal atrophy becomes evident…
posts.post_content: In infectious bursal disease, atrophy of the bursa of Fabricius typically becomes evident how many days after infection?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 3-8 days

Bursal atrophy in IBD typically becomes evident 3-8 days after infection.

Correct Option Explanation

The bursa is initially enlarged, oedematous and cream coloured before undergoing atrophy within this window.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • 10-14, 20-25 and 30-35 days do not match the described early gross timeline.
Know More
  • Haemorrhage may be seen on internal and serosal bursal surfaces.
  • A caseous core can form in the bursal lumen from sloughed epithelium.
  • Muscular haemorrhage in thigh and pectoral muscles is typical of IBD.
  • Kidneys may show swelling, urate deposition and tubule dilation.

posts.post_title: Which IBD test uses macerated bursal tissue…
posts.post_content: Which serological test used in infectious bursal disease diagnosis employs macerated bursal tissue as the antigen source?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Agar gel precipitin test

The agar gel precipitin test (AGPT) uses macerated bursa as antigen in IBD diagnosis.

Correct Option Explanation

ELISA against a known positive antiserum is also used alongside AGPT for serological diagnosis.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • HI and virus neutralisation are not the macerated-bursa antigen tests described for IBD.
  • The tuberculin test is unrelated, used for avian tuberculosis diagnosis.
Know More
  • Immunoperoxidase staining detects antigen in bursal sections.
  • Immunofluorescence is done on frozen bursal sections or smears.
  • Virus isolation is rarely used, being time consuming.
  • Nucleic acid probes and RT-PCR are also diagnostic options.

posts.post_title: Which condition is listed as a differential…
posts.post_content: Which of the following is listed as a differential diagnosis for infectious bursal disease?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Coccidiosis

Coccidiosis is listed among the differential diagnoses for infectious bursal disease.

Correct Option Explanation

Other differentials include Ranikhet disease, haemorrhagic muscle syndrome, avitaminosis A and excess renal urates.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Marek's disease, fowl pox and colibacillosis are not named in the IBD differential list.
Know More
  • FLKS (fatty liver kidney syndrome) is also a listed differential.
  • Water deprivation with swollen kidneys mimics IBD renal signs.
  • Diagnosis often needs history, signs and gross lesions together.
  • Subclinical IBD particularly needs differential work-up.

posts.post_title: Delaying ND vaccination to 2-3 weeks avoids…
posts.post_content: Delaying Newcastle disease vaccination until the second or third week of life is recommended chiefly to:

_aimcq_options.text: Avoid maternal antibody interference with active immunity
Reduce the overall cost of the vaccine
Prevent egg transmission of the vaccine virus
Increase virus shedding from vaccinated birds

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Avoid maternal antibody interference with active immunity

Delaying vaccination avoids maternal antibody interference with an active immune response.

Correct Option Explanation

Healthy chicks may be vaccinated as early as day 1-4, but delay improves immune response development.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Cost reduction, egg transmission prevention and shedding increase are not the stated reason for delay.
Know More
  • Mass application methods include drinking water or spray administration.
  • Individual administration can be via nares or conjunctival sac.
  • Concurrent mycoplasma or bacterial infection can aggravate spray vaccine reactions.
  • Oil-adjuvanted inactivated vaccines suit breeders and layers.

posts.post_title: IBV nephrotoxic serotypes are…
posts.post_content: Which infectious bronchitis virus serotypes are described as nephrotoxic?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: T, Gray and Holte

The T, Gray and Holte serotypes of IBV are nephrotoxic.

Correct Option Explanation

These serotypes target the kidneys, unlike the respiratory-tropic serotypes.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Massachusetts and Connecticut are the respiratory-tract serotypes of IBV, not nephrotoxic ones.
  • H120, H52, A and B are not the nephrotoxic serotypes named in the source.
Know More
  • Concurrent infection with more than one IBV serotype can occur.
  • Secondary bacterial infections worsen respiratory-form severity.
  • Renal signs are seen mainly in birds under 10 weeks old.
  • ELISA is the most sensitive serological test for IB.

posts.post_title: IBV '3 R's' mnemonic refers to which systems…
posts.post_content: The infectious bronchitis virus mnemonic '3 R's' refers to its effect on which three systems?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Respiratory, renal, reproductive

IBV affects the respiratory, renal and reproductive systems (3Rs).

Correct Option Explanation

This causes adverse effects on egg production and quality in layers, and weight gain in broilers.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • The nervous system is not among the three systems named for IBV in this mnemonic.
Know More
  • Secondary Mycoplasma or E. coli infection worsens severity.
  • Complications are aggravated by concurrent respiratory infections.
  • Airborne transmission is the common route of spread.
  • New virus appears within 3-4 hours of infection.

posts.post_title: IBV infection in young chicks can cause…
posts.post_content: Infection of young chicks with infectious bronchitis virus can cause abnormal oviduct development leading to which condition in adulthood?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Blind layer

Abnormal oviduct development from early IBV infection can cause the blind layer condition.

Correct Option Explanation

Partial or complete failure of oviduct development follows IBV infection of chicks before sexual maturity.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Cage layer fatigue relates to calcium deficiency, not IBV oviduct damage.
  • Egg peritonitis and oviduct prolapse are not the specific outcome of early-life IBV infection described.
Know More
  • Adult infection more commonly damages the functional oviduct instead.
  • Egg abnormalities include watery albumin and misshapen shells.
  • Egg production quality can fall by more than 50%.
  • Renal form causes swollen, pale kidneys with urate-filled tubules.

posts.post_title: Most sensitive serological test for IB is…
posts.post_content: Among the serological tests used for infectious bronchitis diagnosis, which is described as more sensitive?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: ELISA

ELISA is described as the more sensitive serological test for infectious bronchitis.

Correct Option Explanation

It complements virus neutralisation, immunodiffusion and haemagglutination inhibition in IB diagnosis.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • VN, ID and HI are listed as other serological tests, not the most sensitive one.
Know More
  • Diagnosis also rests on clinical signs and gross or microscopic lesions.
  • Immunofluorescence is another serological option for IB.
  • Air sacs show thickening and opacity as a gross lesion.
  • Caseous plugs may form in the lower trachea and bronchi.

posts.post_title: Nephritic form of IB chiefly affects birds…
posts.post_content: In infectious bronchitis, the nephritic (renal) form of disease chiefly affects birds:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Under 10 weeks of age

The nephritic form of IB chiefly affects young growing birds under 10 weeks old.

Correct Option Explanation

Mortality in this form can reach 30% in its severe presentation.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Over 20 weeks, laying hens only and breeder males only are not the stated age group for the nephritic form.
Know More
  • Respiratory signs are also seen in the nephritic form.
  • Mild forms show little to no mortality.
  • Kidney microscopic lesions include interstitial nephritis and urolithiasis.
  • Young chicks mainly show the respiratory form of disease.

posts.post_title: Two factors predisposing to ILT are…
posts.post_content: Which two factors are described as predisposing chickens to infectious laryngotracheitis?

_aimcq_options.text: Vitamin D deficiency and heat stress
Vitamin E deficiency and cold stress

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Vitamin A deficiency and ammonia

Vitamin A deficiency and ammonia predispose chickens to infectious laryngotracheitis.

Correct Option Explanation

These factors are named alongside concurrent respiratory infections that complicate ILT.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Vitamin D, vitamin E, biotin, heat and cold stress are not the predisposing factors named for ILT.
Know More
  • ILT is an acute viral disease of chickens and pheasants.
  • Spread occurs by aerosol, ingestion, mechanical carriers and fomites.
  • Concurrent ND, IB, fowl pox or coryza complicate the disease.
  • All age groups are susceptible, including very young chicks.

posts.post_title: In peracute ILT, birds typically show…
posts.post_content: In the peracute form of infectious laryngotracheitis, birds typically show:

_aimcq_options.text: Death without warning signs, or severe dyspnoea with bloody exudate
Mild moist rales and head shaking only
No clinical signs at all in the flock

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Death without warning signs, or severe dyspnoea with bloody exudate

Peracute ILT causes sudden death or severe dyspnoea with bloody exudate.

Correct Option Explanation

Coughing and expectoration of bloody exudate accompany the severe respiratory distress in this form.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Mild moist rales and head shaking describe the mild form, not peracute ILT.
  • No signs at all describes the asymptomatic form; chronic wasting is not an ILT presentation.
Know More
  • The acute form causes death in 3-4 days or recovery in 2-3 weeks.
  • The acute form shows obstruction of trachea with bloody exudate.
  • The asymptomatic form goes unnoticed in a flock.
  • Peracute lesions show haemorrhagic tracheitis causing obstruction.

posts.post_title: Confirmatory diagnosis of ILT relies on…
posts.post_content: Confirmatory diagnosis of infectious laryngotracheitis relies on demonstration of:

_aimcq_options.text: Intranuclear inclusion bodies in tracheal epithelium

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Intranuclear inclusion bodies in tracheal epithelium

ILT diagnosis relies on demonstrating intranuclear inclusion bodies in tracheal epithelium.

Correct Option Explanation

Serological tests such as FAT, IP, ELISA, PCR, AGID, VN and IFA also support diagnosis.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Bollinger bodies are intracytoplasmic and are characteristic of fowl pox, not ILT.
  • Negri bodies and elementary bodies are unrelated to ILT diagnosis.
Know More
  • Virus can also be isolated on the chorioallantoic membrane (CAM).
  • Inclusion bodies are seen in the early stage of infection.
  • Syncytium formation is seen from aggregation of sloughed epithelium.
  • Degenerative changes include swollen cells and loss of cilia.

posts.post_title: Intranuclear inclusions in ILT seen mainly…
posts.post_content: Intranuclear inclusion bodies in infectious laryngotracheitis are seen mainly during which period of infection?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Early stage (1-5 days)

Intranuclear inclusions in ILT are seen mainly in the early stage (1-5 days).

Correct Option Explanation

They disappear as the affected epithelial cells desquamate from the tracheal mucosa.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Late stage, recovered birds and asymptomatic carriers are not when inclusions are described as present.
Know More
  • Desquamation combined with capillary rupture causes haemorrhage.
  • Inflammatory changes include lymphocyte and macrophage infiltration.
  • Syncytium forms from aggregated sloughed epithelial cells.
  • Virus can be demonstrated on the chorioallantoic membrane.

posts.post_title: ILT virus spreads mainly by which routes…
posts.post_content: Infectious laryngotracheitis virus spreads mainly by which routes?

_aimcq_options.text: Aerosol, ingestion, mechanical carriers and fomites

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Aerosol, ingestion, mechanical carriers and fomites

ILT spreads by aerosol, ingestion, mechanical carriers and fomites.

Correct Option Explanation

Multiple simultaneous routes explain its rapid spread once introduced into a flock.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Transovarial transmission alone, biting insects alone, and contaminated feed alone each describe only one of several actual routes.
Know More
  • Concurrent ND, IB, fowl pox and coryza complicate the disease.
  • Vitamin A deficiency and ammonia predispose birds to infection.
  • All age groups are susceptible, especially very young chicks.
  • Serological tests include FAT, IP, ELISA, PCR, AGID, VN and IFA.

posts.post_title: Fowl pox virus is unusual among DNA…
posts.post_content: Fowl pox virus is unusual among DNA viruses in being able to:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Replicate within the cell cytoplasm

Fowl pox virus unusually replicates within the cell cytoplasm.

Correct Option Explanation

It is the largest virus known in birds, with a double-stranded DNA genome.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Nuclear-only replication, non-avian host restriction and cell-free survival are not features described for fowl pox virus.
Know More
  • Complete virions (Borrel granules) accumulate within Bollinger bodies.
  • The virus resists desiccation once inside a scab.
  • Virus does not penetrate intact skin; a break is required for entry.
  • Direct contact during vaccination is a major factor in spread.

posts.post_title: Borrel granules accumulate within which…
posts.post_content: In fowl pox, complete virions known as Borrel granules accumulate within which structures?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Bollinger bodies

Complete virions (Borrel granules) accumulate within Bollinger bodies in fowl pox.

Correct Option Explanation

These eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusion bodies are seen under light microscopy in infected epithelium.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • LCL (Levinthal, Coles, Lillie) bodies are the inclusions seen in avian chlamydiosis, not fowl pox.
  • Negri and Guarnieri bodies are inclusion bodies of other, unrelated viral diseases.
Know More
  • Hyperplasia of epithelium is the most important microscopic lesion.
  • Cell-mediated immunity develops earlier than humoral immunity.
  • Inclusions may occupy the entire cytoplasm, causing cell necrosis.
  • The virus does not penetrate intact, unbroken skin.

posts.post_title: Besides direct contact, fowl pox spreads by…
posts.post_content: Besides direct contact, fowl pox virus is commonly spread by:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Biting insects such as mosquitoes

Biting insects, such as mosquitoes, commonly spread fowl pox virus.

Correct Option Explanation

Aerosols from feather follicles and dried scabs also carry the virus in a contaminated environment.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Waterborne, transovarial and long-distance airborne spread are not routes described for fowl pox.
Know More
  • Direct contact is the major factor in fowl pox transmission.
  • Vaccination can transfer virus between affected and healthy birds.
  • Virus entering the eye reaches the larynx via the lachrymal duct.
  • The disease can also be transmitted by the respiratory tract.

posts.post_title: The two principal clinical forms of fowl pox…
posts.post_content: The two principal clinical forms of fowl pox are the cutaneous form and the:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Diphtheritic (wet) form

The two forms of fowl pox are the cutaneous (dry) form and the diphtheritic (wet) form.

Correct Option Explanation

The diphtheritic form produces fibrino-necrotic lesions in the mucous membranes of the upper respiratory and digestive tract.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Nervous, nephrotic and septicaemic forms are not recognised presentations of fowl pox.
Know More
  • Cutaneous lesions progress from papule to vesicle to scab to scar.
  • Diphtheritic mortality can be as high as 50%, though usually low.
  • Diphtheritic lesions in the larynx cause difficulty in breathing.
  • Diphtheritic lesions in the conjunctiva can cause blindness.

posts.post_title: Cutaneous fowl pox diagnosis confirmed by…
posts.post_content: In the cutaneous form of fowl pox, diagnosis is readily confirmed by demonstrating:

_aimcq_options.text: Intracytoplasmic eosinophilic inclusion bodies (Borrel bodies) in scrapings
Intranuclear basophilic inclusions in the liver
Acid-fast bacilli in bone marrow smears
Spirochaetes in blood smears by dark-field microscopy

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Intracytoplasmic eosinophilic inclusion bodies (Borrel bodies) in scrapings

Cutaneous fowl pox is confirmed by Borrel bodies seen in lesion scrapings.

Correct Option Explanation

Scrapings are made into smears on glass slides and examined with a suitable stain under the microscope.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Basophilic hepatic inclusions relate to inclusion body hepatitis, not fowl pox.
  • Acid-fast bacilli and spirochaetes are diagnostic features of tuberculosis and spirochaetosis, not fowl pox.
Know More
  • The diphtheritic form is harder to diagnose from clinical signs alone.
  • Ulcer formation on lesion removal helps differentiate it from ILT.
  • Serological tests include AGPT, passive haemagglutination and ELISA.
  • An inoculation test can identify inclusion bodies by light microscopy.

posts.post_title: Avian influenza viruses belong to which…
posts.post_content: Avian influenza viruses belong to which virus family group?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Type A orthomyxoviruses

Avian influenza viruses are type A orthomyxoviruses.

Correct Option Explanation

They share antigenically homologous nucleoprotein and matrix internal proteins detected by AGID tests.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Type B paramyxoviruses, type C coronaviruses and type A retroviruses are not the classification of AI viruses.
Know More
  • Most AI viruses are of low pathogenicity (LP) for poultry.
  • The highly pathogenic form was historically called fowl plague.
  • Most wild bird infections with AI viruses are subclinical.
  • Depopulation and quarantine control emerging HP virus outbreaks.

posts.post_title: AI viruses are divided into how many H…
posts.post_content: Avian influenza viruses are divided into how many haemagglutinin and neuraminidase subtypes respectively?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 15 haemagglutinin and 9 neuraminidase subtypes

AI viruses have 15 H and 9 N subtypes based on inhibition tests.

Correct Option Explanation

These are identified by haemagglutination inhibition and neuraminidase inhibition tests respectively.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • The reversed, equal, and smaller subtype counts do not match the actual 15 H and 9 N figures.
Know More
  • Most H1-15 subtypes are of low pathogenicity (LP).
  • Some H5 and H7 subtypes are highly pathogenic (HP).
  • HP viruses arise from mutation of certain H5/H7 LP viruses.
  • LP viruses are common in migrating waterfowl and shorebirds.

posts.post_title: HPAI typically arises from mutation of…
posts.post_content: Highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses typically arise through mutation of low pathogenicity strains of which subtypes?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: H5 and H7

HPAI viruses typically arise through mutation of some low pathogenicity H5 and H7 strains.

Correct Option Explanation

These mutated strains can then cause devastating epizootics in gallinaceous poultry.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • H1/H3, H9/H6 and H2/H4 are not the subtypes described as the source of HP mutants.
Know More
  • Depopulation and quarantine are used to eliminate HP viruses quickly.
  • Incubation period ranges from a few days to one week.
  • HP disease causes cyanosis and oedema of the comb and wattle.
  • Survivors may show CNS signs such as torticollis or incoordination.

posts.post_title: AI haemagglutination differs from ND by…
posts.post_content: Avian influenza virus haemagglutination in embryonated eggs is distinguished from Newcastle disease virus because it is:

posts.post_content: Which management practice helps control cannibalism and feather picking in poultry flocks?

_aimcq_options.text: Beak trimming with reduced light intensity and adequate space

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Beak trimming with reduced light intensity and adequate space

Beak trimming, reduced light intensity and adequate space help control cannibalism.

Correct Option Explanation

Ensuring balanced nutrition alongside these measures further reduces the risk of pecking-related outbreaks.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Increasing stocking density, increasing light intensity and withholding feed for extended periods would worsen, not control, cannibalism risk.
Know More
  • Overcrowding, bright light and nutritional deficiencies commonly trigger outbreaks.
  • Feather picking often precedes and can progress to true cannibalism.
  • Nutritional deficiencies, such as low protein or salt, can contribute.
  • Prompt removal of injured birds can help limit further pecking.
